speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you tell me when you first noticed the lesion on your leg and if you have experienced any recent trauma or insect bites in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and anterior uveitis, I need to determine if this is a systemic manifestation; does the lesion have a raised, indurated border resembling a boil or abscess? I would like to perform a physical examination of the lesion and your joints to check for any signs of arthritis or other systemic inflammation.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of trauma at the site, combined with the painful ulcer and your history of Crohn's disease, strongly suggests Pyoderma Gangrenosum. I will request a biopsy to confirm this and rule out infection or vasculitis. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
